title: First jazz records and Texas versus New Orleans
summary: First jazz records he recalls: Louisiana Five, Original Dixieland Band, Ted Lewis; he thought Texas bands were as good.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Oh, back in your early days, what were the first records you remember that sounded like jazz to you?

Well, I think the very first record I remember was Louisiana Five. They had, uh, Al Nunez, who had clarinet. It was a five-piece band, just clarinet and rhythm. And I think he had trombone. I don't remember who it was. Then, uh, the original Dixeland Jazz Band was very fine. And, uh, then, uh, I remember Ted Lewis. I remember Ted Lewis, as you know, was probably a little different style. But, uh, he was one of the first jazz bands on record anyway.
That mighty fine trombone playing with it, too. Yes.

Mm-hmm. But we were playing, uh, I don't know, uh, we were playing just the same over with Peck. Of course, Peck was a better pianist, and, uh, so, uh, maybe we had an edge on, on the Dixeland band in that respect. But, uh, and I know that I played practically the same trombone as I do now. Uh, I think that things were going, uh, more or less in, uh, from the Texas side, just about as good as they were over here.
